title: Jinn Simplify
description: Hourly, deliberately high-effort simplification pipeline for Jinn. Surveys one worthwhile target, fixes a mechanical budget before code, allows two bounded implementation rounds, gates delivery on CI, and never asks for approval.

config.prompt:
SURVEY PHASE — find one simplification worth an expensive run. Do not change code.

Work against the current Jinn repository at `~/Projects/jinn` and inspect real code before deciding.

First use `gh pr list --state open --json headRefName` to count open PRs whose head branch begins `simplify/`. The queue ceiling is 5 open `simplify/*` PRs. If the count is 5 or greater, decline immediately with `worth: no`, report the count in evidence, and do not create a Todo.

Then query existing Todos carrying the `simplify` label across open states and recently closed work. Skip every area already covered by an existing `simplify` Todo; do not rename the same idea to evade that check. If two or more `simplify` Todos are already executing, decline this run.

Enumerate the relevant core pieces — Todos, Workflows, Triggers, Sessions, Employees, Engines, Connectors, Cron, Knowledge, gateway HTTP, and web UI — then select exactly ONE evidence-backed target from:
1. over-engineering that can be deleted;
2. blended concerns that should be separated, especially vocabulary or storage confused across core pieces;
3. a real dead path, swallowed failure, or behaviour that no longer matches its prose.

Prefer deletion and clearer ownership. Do not manufacture work merely because the schedule fired. If no target is clearly worth the token cost, submit `worth: no` and do not create a Todo.

When and only when the target is worthwhile:
- call `create_work_item` with a specific title, evidence and intended outcome, and `labels: ["simplify"]`;
- move that Todo to `executing` so the ledger reflects active work;
- return its canonical ID as `todoId` and return `worth: yes`.

Do not write code, create a branch, or create a worktree in this phase.

## Production safety — absolute
- NEVER use port 7777 or touch `~/.jinn`.
- NEVER start or run a gateway without BOTH an explicit throwaway `JINN_HOME` and an explicit non-production port. Port 7788 is also forbidden.
- Before starting a throwaway daemon, inspect its config and confirm its port is neither 7777 nor 7788.
- NEVER kill a process you did not start.
- The public repository must stay generic: no real names, project or client names, emails, keys, Slack IDs, or personal absolute paths.

## Browser isolation
Before any browser command, export `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE` to a unique disposable directory under `~/.agent-browser/profiles/jinn-simplify-<run-id>-<phase>`.
Use `agent-browser` only; never raw headless Chrome and never drive Playwright by hand. Delete the disposable profile directory when browser work ends.

worth.description: Exactly `yes` when one target is worth pursuing; otherwise `no`.

todoId.description: Canonical ID of the created simplify Todo. Omit when worth is no.

target.description: The one selected code area, or a concise reason the run was declined.

evidence.description: Concrete files, callers, failures, queue count, or vocabulary proving the choice.

config.prompt:
CONSTRAIN PHASE — freeze a mechanical simplification budget before code changes.

Todo: {{ node.survey.fields.todoId }}
Target: {{ node.survey.fields.target }}
Evidence: {{ node.survey.fields.evidence }}

Read the Todo, the shared Jinn taste rules through the company knowledge tools, and the implicated repository code. Turn the target into a small, testable plan. The model that writes this budget will not implement it.

Run `git fetch origin` first. Resolve the fetched remote tip with `git rev-parse origin/main` and emit that exact full SHA as `baseHead`. Create an isolated worktree at `~/Projects/.worktrees/jinn-simplify-{{ node.survey.fields.todoId }}` on branch `simplify/{{ node.survey.fields.todoId }}-<short-slug>` from that captured `origin/main` SHA. Never cut the worktree from local `main`. Never reuse, delete, reset, clean, or repurpose an unrelated worktree. Write `PLAN.md` there before any product-code edit.

Declare all budget fields. Defaults require explicit evidence to relax:
- `netLineDelta` must be 0 or negative.
- `maxFilesTouched` must be a small integer.
- `maxNewFiles` must be 0 unless splitting an oversized file is the task.
- `maxFileLines` is an absolute post-change cap; no touched file may grow.
- no new dependencies, config options, public exports, or single-caller abstractions.
- preserve behaviour with `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build`; delete a test only when the behaviour it covered is deleted.

Emit `budgetCommand` as one literal, non-destructive shell command the verifiers can run from the worktree. It must print the real net line delta, touched-file count, new-file count, and maximum line count among touched files against the captured base SHA. Do not use placeholders in the emitted command.

Emit `acceptance` as a numbered, mechanical checklist including the qualitative constraints above. The plan and output must agree.

Do not edit product code. Stop honestly if isolation or a checkable budget cannot be established.

## Browser isolation
Before any browser command, export `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE` to a unique disposable directory under `~/.agent-browser/profiles/jinn-simplify-<run-id>-<phase>`.
Use `agent-browser` only; never raw headless Chrome and never drive Playwright by hand. Delete the disposable profile directory when browser work ends.

config.prompt:
DELIVER PHASE — publish verified work for operator review. Do not merge.

Todo {{ node.survey.fields.todoId }}. Worktree `{{ node.constrain.fields.worktree }}`. Branch `{{ node.constrain.fields.branch }}`. Plan `{{ node.constrain.fields.planPath }}`.

Re-run the exact `{{ node.constrain.fields.budgetCommand }}` plus `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build`. Stop if the branch moved beyond the verified head or any local check fails.

Push the branch with `git push -u origin {{ node.constrain.fields.branch }}`. Open the pull request as a draft with `gh pr create --draft --base main --head {{ node.constrain.fields.branch }}`. The PR body must give the selected area, evidence of over-engineering or blended concerns, the fixed constraint budget, the reconciled measured budget output including any verified contract defect, what was deleted or clarified, and the test results.

After the PR exists, wait for the complete CI result with `gh pr checks --watch`. If any job is red, re-run each red job once and only once, then wait for the complete CI result again. If every job is green after the initial run or the single re-run, mark the PR ready, set `checksStatus: green`, move the Todo to `in_review`, and add a concise Todo comment with the PR URL and measured budget.

If a job fails again, the failure is reproducible: leave or convert the PR to draft, set `checksStatus: reproducible-failure`, move the Todo to `escalated`, and add the failing job plus its final evidence to both the PR and Todo. Do not present a reproducibly red PR as ready. Do not merge or close the Todo.

## Production safety — absolute
- NEVER use port 7777 or touch `~/.jinn`.
- NEVER start or run a gateway without BOTH an explicit throwaway `JINN_HOME` and an explicit non-production port. Port 7788 is also forbidden.

config.prompt:
HAND BACK — two implementation rounds did not converge. Do not fix code and do not start another round.

Todo {{ node.survey.fields.todoId }}. Branch `{{ node.constrain.fields.branch }}` remains in `{{ node.constrain.fields.worktree }}`.

Unresolved findings:
{{ node.verify-2.fields.findings }}
Final budget verdict: {{ node.verify-2.fields.budgetVerdict }}

First call `update_work_item` for the Todo with status `escalated`. Then add one concise Todo comment stating what was attempted, what remains blocked, the real budget status, and the single decision that would unblock the operator. Leave the branch and worktree intact. Do not push, open a PR, merge, or close the Todo.
